topic: The Wallis Product: Unveiling Pi through Infinite Fractions
target_audience: Undergraduate students or advanced high school students with a basic understanding of calculus.

sections.title: The Hook: Finding Pi without a Compass
lecture_lines: A circle's area reveals the mysterious constant pi.
Halving it starts a sequence of simple ratios.
This infinite product converges exactly to pi halves.
animations: Fade in a bright blue circle (#58C4DD) with 'Area = pi' (#FFFFFF) inside.
The circle morphs into 'pi/2' (#FFFFFF) while the start of the Wallis sequence '2/1 * 2/3' appears (#F4D03F).
A sequence of ratios grows horizontally (2/1 * 2/3 * 4/3...), while the decimal value 1.5707 (#FFFFFF) appears and updates.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Wallis Integrals
lecture_lines: We define the integral of sine to the nth power.
The first power forms a broad, sweeping wave.
Squaring the sine causes the area to shrink.
Higher powers compress the curve into a narrow spike.
This specific area is labeled as I sub n.
animations: Display the integral I_n = integral from 0 to pi/2 of sin^n(x) dx in white (#FFFFFF).
Plot y = sin(x) in orange (#FF7043) and shade the area under it.
Transition the curve to y = sin^2(x) in yellow (#F4D03F) and update the shading.
Transition the curve to y = sin^10(x) in blue (#2196F3), showing the area narrowing to a spike.
Label the shaded area as 'I_n' and make it pulse in white (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: The Reduction Step: Building the Staircase
lecture_lines: Integration by parts reveals a helpful recurrence relation.
This creates a downward staircase of integral values.
Each step down multiplies by a specific fraction.
animations: Show 'Integration by Parts' text and the formula I_n = ((n-1)/n) * I_{n-2} in white (#FFFFFF).
Create a vertical staircase of steps labeled I_n, I_{n-2}, I_{n-4} in white (#FFFFFF) incorporating the stair icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/stair.svg].
Animate a jump from I_4 to I_2 with the fraction '3/4' appearing as a multiplier in light blue (#58C4DD).

sections.title: Even vs. Odd: The Convergence Logic
lecture_lines: We separate the integrals into even and odd sequences.
These two sequences develop side by side.
Comparing their ratios is the key to convergence.
As n grows, the ratio approaches exactly one.
This squeeze effect forces the sequences to merge.
animations: Display sequences (I_0, I_2, I_4) and (I_1, I_3, I_5) in two distinct columns in light blue (#58C4DD).
Draw horizontal connecting lines between I_{2n} and I_{2n-1} terms in white (#FFFFFF).
Write the ratio 'I_{2n} / I_{2n-1}' in yellow (#F4D03F) between the sequences.
Animate the ratio expression transforming into '-> 1' in yellow (#F4D03F).
Display the inequality I_{2n} > I_{2n+1} > I_{2n+2} in orange (#FF7043) to illustrate the squeeze effect.

sections.title: The Final Product: Piecing it Together
lecture_lines: Combine the even and odd terms to isolate pi.
Fractions from both sequences begin to intertwine.
Rearranging these terms creates a chain of ratios.
We arrive at the elegant Wallis Product formula.
The value slowly approaches one point five seven.
animations: Display the product expansions for I_{2n} and I_{2n+1} in white (#FFFFFF) and light blue (#58C4DD).
Rearrange the terms into the ratio I_{2n}/I_{2n+1}, isolating pi/2 in yellow (#F4D03F).
Assemble the resulting fraction product (2/1 * 2/3 * 4/3 * 4/5...) like connected blocks [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/blocks.svg] (#58C4DD).
Surround the complete Wallis Product formula with a bold white rectangular frame (#FFFFFF).
Show a decimal counter starting at 2.0 and smoothly changing to 1.5707 in yellow (#F4D03F).

sections.title: Application: Why It Matters
lecture_lines: This product links to Stirling's approximation of factorials.
It even appears in the physics of hydrogen atoms.
Simple fractions reveal the universe's hidden mathematical clockwork.
animations: Fade in the Wallis formula alongside Stirling's formula (n! ≈ sqrt(2πn)(n/e)^n) in white (#FFFFFF).
Show a blue Bohr atom model [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/atom.svg] (#58C4DD) and a green Bell Curve (#4CAF50).
